candidates.title: [Bug]: xml:elements / xml:elementChildren panic "invalid XML element name filter" when the name matches no element
candidates.body: ### Description `xml:elements(nm)` and `xml:elementChildren(nm)` panic with `invalid XML element name filter` when `nm` is not a parsable expanded name (e.g. `"ns:a"`, `""`, `"p:t"`, `"{}a"`) or is in the xmlns namespace, instead of returning an empty sequence. ### Steps to Reproduce ```ballerina import ballerina/io; public function main() { xml x = xml `t`; io:println(x.elements("ns:a").length()); // @output 0 io:println(x.elements("").length()); // @output 0 io:println(x.elementChildren("p:t").length()); // @output 0 io:println(x.elements("a")); // @output } ``` Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run .bal`. **Actual:** ``` error: invalid XML element name filter at main(lang-xml-elements-unmatched-name-v.bal:5) ``` **Expected:** ``` 0 0 0 ``` **Spec reasoning:** lang.xml documents `elements(xml x, string? nm = ()) returns xml` as returning "an xml sequence consisting of all the element items in `x` whose expanded name is `nm`" (and `elementChildren` likewise "include only elements whose expanded name is `nm`"). The return type has no error and no panic is documented; it is a pure filter. No element can have expanded name `ns:a`, `""` or `p:t`, so the result is an empty sequence. jBallerina just compares names and returns empty. Both functions are listed as supported in subset10.md. Likely origin: `selectedElements` in `lib/langlibs/go/lang.xml/xml.go` panics when `ParseExpandedXMLName` fails or the URI is the xmlns namespace. ### Affected Version(s) main @ 0082563 ### OS, DB, other environment details and versions nutcracker built from `ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina` main @ 008256345f394cc66d5cab6f0409101709094b27 (`go run ./cli/cmd run `), Linux x86_64. ### Related area Runtime

candidates.title: [Bug]: member access evaluates the key expression before the container expression
[Bug]: range expression in a const declaration crashes the compiler (INTERNAL_ERROR: unsupported constant binary operator ..<)
candidates.body:
Another crash path for a range expression used as a value: a module **const** declaration. It fails in a different place than the reproducers here. The crash is in constant evaluation during semantic analysis, `semantics/internal/types/constant_evaluator.go` (the default branch of the constant binary-operator switch), not in BIR generation. A fix in birgen alone won't cover it.

```ballerina
const A = 1 ..< 3; // @error

public function main() {
    _ = A;
}
```

Actual (main @ 0082563):
```
fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: unsupported constant binary operator ..<
 --> bug2-e.bal:1:11
  |
1 | const A = 1 ..< 3; // @error
  |           ^^^^^^^
```
`const A = 1 ... 3;` and the nested `const B = [1 ... 3];` crash the same way (`unsupported constant binary operator ...`).

Expected: an ordinary diagnostic, not INTERNAL_ERROR. §6.4 lists `range-expr` in the `const-expr` grammar, but §8 module-const-decl requires the constant's value to be anydata (its type is readonly & the singleton shape). A range expression produces an `Iterable<int,()>` object (§6.26), so this should be a normal semantic error.

(I also re-checked that the original reproducers here, `var r = 1 ..< 3;` and `object {} r = 1 ..< 3;`, still crash with `unexpected binary operator kind: ..<` on current main.)
